plan.topic: Tirzepatide and the gallbladder: how often gallbladder problems (gallstones, gallbladder inflammation) were reported in the SURMOUNT-1 trial, why rapid weight loss raises gallstone risk, and the warning signs on the label
plan.angle: Gallbladder problems were uncommon in the trial data. Gallstones were reported at a similar rate on tirzepatide and placebo (about 1 in 100). Gallbladder inflammation was less common, but it showed up more on tirzepatide (0.7% vs 0.2%). Quote the exact source (the NEJM SURMOUNT-1 supplement or the label) and its population, 'without diabetes'. Then: fast weight loss by any method is linked to gallstones. Give the label's warning signs and 'tell your healthcare provider right away'. Add 'Don't stop or change your medicines on your own', 'Not personal advice' and the prescriber line.
plan.working_title: Tirzepatide and Your Gallbladder: How Common Are Problems?
plan.why: The playbook's 08:00 body-worry slot (our top Instagram format) with tirzepatide in the title. The evidence is settled trial and label data, and gallbladder hasn't been covered in the last 30 days. | fact-check: The figures the label reports don't support 'more frequent on tirzepatide' as a blanket claim. Cholelithiasis (gallstones) was about 1.1% on tirzepatide vs 1.0% on placebo, which is essentially similar. Cholecystitis (gallbladder inflammation) was 0.7% vs 0.2%, and cholecystectomy 0.2% vs 0%. The label figures may be pooled across trials, so either take per-arm SURMOUNT-1 numbers from the NEJM 2022 supplement or say 'in the Zepbound label's trial data'. Don't present pooled figures as SURMOUNT-1. The label's urgency wording is 'tell your healthcare provider right away'. Use that word for word, with the four symptoms (upper-stomach pain, fever, yellowing of skin or eyes, clay-colored stools). Source: https://medical.lilly.com/us/products/answers/can-people-with-gallbladder-disease-or-gallbladder-removal-take-zepbound-tirzepatide-266122

Losing weight quickly (including after weight-loss surgery) is linked to gallstones.

factcheck.summary:
I checked every figure and found them accurate. Lilly Medical's page (last reviewed 28 Jan 2025) confirms the pooled SURMOUNT-1 and SURMOUNT-2 rates: gallstones (cholelithiasis) 1.1% on tirzepatide vs 1% on placebo, gallbladder inflammation (cholecystitis) 0.7% vs 0.2%, and gallbladder removal (cholecystectomy) 0.2% vs none on placebo. The population wording is right too: adults with obesity or overweight, with SURMOUNT-2 enrolling people with type 2 diabetes.

The four symptoms and "tell your healthcare provider right away" match the Zepbound Medication Guide word for word. I confirmed that wording through a search result quoting the guide; the PDF itself wouldn't extract.

NIDDK supports the point that fast weight loss, including after weight-loss surgery, is linked to gallstones, and the script keeps it as "linked to" rather than "causes".

Safety is covered: the "don't stop or change your medicines" line, "Not personal advice" and the prescriber line are all there. The script gives absolute rates throughout, keeps the less reassuring inflammation number in, and pays off the title. It's about 150 words and the "follow for more" CTA is correct because no long-form is named.

Only minor polish is needed: three on-screen stat texts don't name the comparator or the organ for muted viewers, and the trial timeframe isn't spoken.

One more thing to know: I couldn't open the two Lilly PDFs (src2, src2b) to read them. src2b's wording is confirmed indirectly through the search result. For src2 I checked only that the URL exists, so its section 5 numbers are confirmed through src1, not by reading the label.

audio.soundNotes: Measured levels were already close to target (music -13.5 dB under voice, -12.6 in pauses), so I trimmed music_gain to 0.85 for extra masking headroom on a Short with a history of masking holds. Thinned redundant simultaneous whoosh/tick layers at the two reveal transitions (6s, 12s) and at the two tick-duplicate moments (53.7s, 61.7s), and pulled down two loud transition swooshes that were sitting over speech at -7.9 and -9.5 dB (cues 21, 34) to the felt -14/-20 dB speech range. Slightly softened the "hit" accent under the serious "tell your provider right away" line to keep that moment calm rather than alarming, per the dramatic-moment thinning rule.
